findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Crepes, apples, and hollendaise sauce were all in different stages of the cooling process in the walk-in cooler. Crepes were separated out to allow for quicker chilling on multiple plates after one stack was observed with an internal temperature of 67F and the other an internal temperature of 83F. Crepes were within the last half hour of the 2hr timeframe for cooling. Hollendaise sauce after stirring was observed with internal temperatures of 83F and 87F. Containers were in a tub of water that consisted of a melted ice bath. Owner added more ice to the container, and based on information provided the hollendaise sauce had another hour to reach 70F/below. Apples had an internal temperature of 127F and were placed in the melted ice bath more recently. Best practices were discussed, including but not limited to separating cooling foods into multiple batches in ice baths to quickly chill foods and ensuring foods are stirred and rotated frequently to aid in chilling process. The importance of monitoring time and temperature of cooling foods was also reiterated. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 (B) Upon arrival inspector observed the facility dish temp tester reading at 175F surface temperate as of the last cycle checked (~5 -10 minutes prior). Final rinse surface temperature during inspection was initially observed at 149F-151F with inspector and facility dish temp testers. The rinse gauge was not moving past 110F, and the booster heater needed to be reset. Rinse gauge continued to sit at 110F. Refilling the dish machine and running close to a dozen cycles resulted in the final rinse gauge getting to ~185F, with surface rinse temperatures at 159F and 161F according to inspector and facility dish temp testers. Facility dish temp tester would remain in the dish rack for each cycle for the remainder of the day to monitor surface rinse temperature. Employee in dish area was educated on monitoring temperatures and what to do in case the dish machine starts to have issues.
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through equipment that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Plate of cooling crepes in the walk-in cooler had surface temperatures ranging from 55F-72F. Internal temperature was observed at 104F (top of stack), 113F (middle of stack), and 93F (bottom of stack). Crepes were made around 7am, and temperatures were checked after 9am. PIC chose to reheat crepes and restart cooling process. Best practices were discussed. PIC placed reheated crepes on two baking sheets in thin layers on the top shelf in the back of the walk-in cooler to help quickly chill product. 
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portion of deli turkey above the fill line of a container in the top of a prep cooler had internal temperature of 53F. Surface temperature of thick sliced ham was observed at 50F for portion above fill line of container with portions underneath at 40F/below further down in container. Double panning was also occurring for portions of foods due to concerns of freezing. Cease the practice of double panning foods in the top of the prep cooler, and store foods in the walk-in cooler overnight to avoid issues with freezing. Portions of deli meats in question will be served or discarded by the end of business today.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee in dish area washed hands without proper technique and shut off the manual faucet without a barrier prior to drying hands. Fellow employee provided education on proper technique. Proper handwashing was observed for remainder of inspection.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 (B) Upon start of inspection dishes were not getting properly heat sanitized based on initial observation of dish machine rinse gauge, final rinse surface temperature, and the manner in which the cycles were ran. Door to dish machine was opened prior to conclusion of rinse cycle with the gauge reading below 180F, and inspector’s dish temp tester showed a final rinse surface temperature of 144F. It took upwards of a dozen cycles for the dish machine final rinse surface temperature to reach 160F/above despite the rinse gauge reaching temperatures close to 200F during the rinse cycle. Employee in dish area was advised on allowing the dish machine to complete a full cycle and verifying proper heat sanitization prior to ware washing. Dishes that were not properly heat sanitized prior to machine reaching proper rinse temperature were placed through additional ware washing cycles for proper heat sanitization.
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through equipment that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of deli meats were stacked above the fill line of containers in the top of a prep cooler, with some portions spilling out of the containers. Surface temperatures were observed between 58F-60F, and one portion of turkey was observed with internal temperature of 55F. Portions down in the containers were observed with surface temperatures of 37F-42F. Portions were said to be recently stocked. Cook  was advised on stocking pans in the top holding area of prep coolers and to avoid over-filling. Items above the fill line will not be maintained at 41F/below as demonstrated with products today. Portions above the fill line were moved inside the cooler to cold hold until needed. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Gravy was in the process of cooling in the walk-in cooler. Gravy was observed in four plastic 6qt containers full to the top, covered, and stacked together. Surface temperatures were observed at 93F-104F, while internal temperatures in the middle were at 134F-139F. Cook noted the gravy was made around 6:30am, set on the back prep table and held at room temperature briefly prior to placing in a ice bath for ~30 minutes, and placed in the walk-in cooler around 7:00am. Temperatures were not checked during cooling process or prior to placing product in the cooler. Best practices for cooling were discussed. Gravy was removed from walk-in to further portion in multiple containers and place back in ice baths. Multiple portions were observed on the back prep table sitting at room temperature ~20 minutes later. Owner and cook were advised to place cooling portions of gravy on ice baths as soon as possible to allow for rapid chilling. **See general comments for additional information.**
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Broccoli cheddar soup in back hot holding unit was observed with an internal temperature of 130F. Chili and chicken noodle soup in the same unit had internal temperatures above 140F. All products were said to have reached an internal temperature of 170F prior to placing in the hot holding well. Soup was placed on countertop cooker to reheat to 165F. Water in the holding well was at 169F. The hot water was only in contact with the bottom quarter of the soup container, so more hot water was placed in the holding well to better surround the container with hot water.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 1. Raw bacon in back prep area was sitting on prep table and observed with surface temperatures of 46F-56F and internal temperatures of 42F-50F. Bacon was placed back in the walk-in cooler for storage until needed. Ensure TCS foods are placed back in coolers if there is an interruption in prep/cooking and/or if not all the product is needed.
2. Portions of deli meat were stacked above the fill line of a container in one of the small prep coolers. Internal temperature for a top portion of turkey was at 60F, and a portion from the bottom of the container was at 40F. All portions of deli meats were stocked around opening today and top portions will be used or discarded within 6hrs. Cooler was holding below 40F, but products in the top were double panned which can impact cold holding temperatures. Owner was advised to stock smaller portions and monitor temperatures of foods in the top of the cooler to ensure foods are maintained at 41F/below.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 A few employees were observed quickly rinsing hands for a few seconds at the kitchen handwashing sink and not taking time to wash hands fully with proper technique. Proper handwashing was discussed with all employees that were present at the time of inspection. Ensure hands are properly washed and not just quickly rinsed between tasks. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Final rinse temperature gauge was reading around 130F and not reaching 180F after 3 to 4 ware washing cycles. The surface temperature was observed at 154F with inspector’s dish temp tester. PIC realized the booster heater needed to be reset. After resetting the booster heater, the final rinse gauge read between 185F-190F, and the surface temperature was observed at 162F.
After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through equipment that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with food debris, and crevice around the blade had debris and metal shavings. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Sausages in steam table were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 117F to 130F. PIC noted the staff began turning off hot holding units recently to begin the cooling process. Other hot TCS foods were observed at 133F-136F and were immediately placed in an ice bath in the walk-in cooler to begin active cooling. Some sausages were well below 135F, and PIC began to reheat sausages but ultimately decided to discard the product. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Hash browns in the bottom of a prep cooler had surface temperatures at 55F-57F and an internal temperature of 60F. PIC noted the potatoes may have been removed from the cooler for a brief period during lunch service. Time was not being tracked for the in-use supply and it was assumed the intent was to keep the potatoes cold. Potatoes were in the danger zone for an unknown amount of time and were discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Individual portions of thawed vacuum packaged salmon were observed in the bottom of a prep cooler. Other portions in the process of thawing were observed in the walk-in cooler. None of the packages were cut. PIC had employee cut the packages of thawed portions in the prep cooler during inspection. Ensure packaging is cut from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the walk-in cooler. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section (under cold running water).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Facility food thermometer was reading at a lower temperature compared to inspector’s when a hot food temperature was checked. Ice water was setup for calibration, and facility food thermometer was reading around 25F. Thermometer was calibrated to 30F-32F during inspection. PIC stated all food thermometers will be checked for calibration prior to service tomorrow morning. 
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for all employees. Certification was missing for one of the cooks, and the employee in the dish area confirmed they did not have a food handler certification. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) A signed reporting agreement was not available for the employee working in the dish area at the time of inspection. Employee health policy was discussed. Owner had the employee sign a copy of the reporting agreement. Owner stated he would double check to ensure all staff have signed copies on file. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee working in dish area handled soiled dishes and proceeded to handle clean dishes without first washing his hands. Employee was also observed wiping hands on his apron/clothing. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and employee washed his hands prior to handling any more clean dishes. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, between handling soiled and clean equipment and utensils, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Process lasted less than 20 seconds. Cook also began drying hands with dispensed paper towels and then shut off the manual faucet prior to fully drying hands. Cook was advised on proper handwashing. Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. Get new paper towels to finish drying hands if additional drying is needed. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Cook was observed wiping down a knife with a dry wiping cloth. Use of sanitizer solution to wipe the knife between uses was discussed. Ensure utensils have time to to dry prior to next use, and make sure in-use utensils are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Cook was observed wiping down surfaces with a wiping cloth that was said to have come from a sanitizer solution and then proceeded back to food prep and handling ready to eat food without changing his gloves. Proper glove use was discussed. Cook washed his hands and changed gloves prior to continuing with food prep. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of deli meat stacked above the fill line of a container in the small prep cooler had an internal temperature of 58F. A portion in the bottom of the same pan was observed at 33F. Owner was advised on stocking pans in the top holding area of prep coolers and to avoid over-filling. Items above the fill line will not be maintained at 41F/below as demonstrated with products today. All portions of deli meats and other TCS foods stacked above the fill line of containers were to be used or discarded by the end of lunch service. 

TCS foods in the top holding area of the large prep cooler had surface temperatures above 60F. Cheese shreds were observed with internal temperature of 57F-58F. Lids to prep cooler were continuously open to prepare orders. Main cook noted smaller portions of foods were placed in the cooler to ensure products were getting used quickly. All TCS foods in the top of the large prep cooler were to be used or discarded by the end of lunch service.  

Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Tracking sheet for working supplies of time controlled American fries and hashbrowns was observed with a time of 7a for the current operating day. Time was being tracked, but one of the employees later placed the pans in the bottom of a prep cooler. Owner and employee were advised portions of potatoes are to be used or discarded within 4hrs and should not be placed back in cold holding if time control is used. Owner stated leftover portions have been kept at closing time depending on how much product is left. Owner was advised to cease the practice and to remove less product later in the day to ensure less waste. Once foods are removed from cold holding and are held at room temperature as part of the time control policy they are to be served or discarded. Even if it hasn't been a full 4hrs the product must be discarded. Owner stated he understood and would have staff remove less product from the cooler later in the day.
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours, the food shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if ready to eat, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged salmon were observed in the original packaging in the bottom of a prep cooler and in the walkin cooler. Proper thawing of ROP fish was discussed. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section (under cold running water).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Wiping cloth was observed hanging over the side of the sani-bucket used by servers in the dining area. Wiping cloth was placed in sanitizer for proper storage. Ensure staff are placing wiping cloth in buckets for proper submersion in sanitizer between uses.

Wiping cloths observed out on the cook line. At least one wiping cloth was used to wipe off crumbs from a cutting board. Ensure wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer solution between uses.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text:
3-302.15 Food handler was observed preparing orders with produce that was not previously washed. An avocado was cut and strawberries were removed from original container and sliced without first washing. Washing produce prior to use was discussed. Owner had employee wash produce prior to finishing orders.  
Raw fruits and vegetables shall be thoroughly washed in water to remove soil and other contaminants before being cut, combined with other ingredients, cooked, served, or offered for human consumption in ready-to-eat form.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.17 Detergent container was empty at the dish machine. A new container of dish detergent was provided.  
When used for warewashing, the mechanical warewasher shall contain a wash solution of soap, detergent, acid cleaner, alkaline cleaner, degreaser, abrasive cleaner, or other cleaning agent according to the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions.
